faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about user identification in OpenPanel.

items.question: What happens before a user is identified?
items.answer: The visitor is an anonymous device id, computed from user agent, IP and site with a salt that rotates every day. When you call identify, the events from that same session (up to six hours back) are rewritten to the profile, so the sign-up flow becomes part of the person's history. Earlier sessions stay anonymous.

items.question: Is this GDPR-compliant?
items.answer: Yes. You control exactly what data you send. OpenPanel doesn't add tracking pixels, persistent identifiers or third-party cookies. If you self-host, no data ever leaves your infrastructure. You can also delete a user's data at any time to comply with erasure requests.

items.question: How is this different from Google Analytics user tracking?
items.answer: Google Analytics relies on anonymous client IDs and has limited support for individual-level profiles. OpenPanel gives you a dedicated profile page per user with a full event timeline, session history, and custom properties-without sending data to Google.

items.question: Can I attach custom properties to users?
items.answer: Yes. Pass any key-value pairs when you call identify()-plan, company, role, revenue, or anything else. These properties are searchable and can be used to filter and segment users across all reports.

items.question: Do I need to identify every user?
items.answer: No. Identify when someone logs in or signs up. Visitors you never identify stay in the Anonymous tab and still count in funnels, retention and the overview.

items.question: Can I merge two identities?
items.answer: Not yet. There is no alias call, so two profile ids stay two profiles and nothing is merged across devices. Use a stable id from your own system, such as the user id from your database, and call identify with it on every device the person logs in on.
